pairs.subject: candidate-consent-and-retention
pairs.evidence: app/_lib/consent.ts:68 A consent that was granted but has no expiry is treated as active forever, so PII keeps flowing and the sweep (which filters on consent_expires_at IS NOT NULL) never reaches it; with no 'withdrawn' status either, the lifecycle has an indefinite-hoard path and no route for withdrawal.

techniques.evidence: app/_lib/consent.ts:38 The gate itself is right: consentWithholdsPii is the control and the sweep is only an optimisation, and an unparseable expiry fails closed. But there is no withdrawn state, so the predicate cannot withhold on withdrawal. A granted consent with a missing expiry serves PII (line 68), whereas the technique says a missing state must withhold. Callers also apply the gate one by one (about 20 call sites) instead of at a single projection layer.

app/_lib/consent.ts:29 The disclosed months are computed from the same TTL that enforcement reads and rounded up, so the disclosure cannot under-state the window. A bad env value falls back to the 365-day default, never to zero or 'no retention'. Two minor points: the deployment is not told when the fallback fires, and the sweep interval is not added into the ceiling.

app/_lib/erasure-full-scrub.test.ts:257 Every table in the tenancy manifest must either be written by the erasure code or be exempted with a stated reason, and a test enforces this. anonymizeEntry runs as one .immediate() transaction scoped to the workspace, re-asserts anonymized_at IS NULL so a second erasure is a no-op, deletes audio files only after commit, and masks the name copied onto audit events. Analyses are matched on a trimmed, lower-cased label within the workspace.

app/_lib/consent.ts:250 scrubPiiFromPayload works from a deny-list: a key that is not in PII_KEYS, PII_ARRAY_KEYS or PII_CONTAINER_KEYS is kept and recursed into, not redacted. Free-text keys it does not name (summary, rationale, notes inside an analysis payload) survive. That is the 'protect what someone remembered' default the technique rejects. Named containers are deep-redacted, and a corrupt payload is replaced with {} (correct).

app/_lib/consent.ts:160 The mask keeps the full first name plus the surname initial ('Zdenka P.'), not initials. In a small cohort that handle can identify the person. The stoplist, the safe fallback and the single-token handling all match the technique; the retained shell keeps scores and stage.

app/_lib/db/pipeline.ts:2443 The carve-out is listed by record type with a stated ground, but it has no end date. No code deletes decision_records except the simulation store, so the exemption keeps them indefinitely, which is the 'unbounded carve-out' failure.

pairs.registryProposal: The read-time-gate technique handles absent-by-design (never asked) and absent-by-corruption, but not a third case found here: a legacy grant from before expiry dates existed, with no expiry recorded. It should say explicitly whether such rows need a backfilled expiry (for example grant date + default TTL) instead of staying active forever.

pairs.subject: candidate-consent-and-retention
pairs.evidence: app/data/[token]/DataClient.tsx:216 The erasure receipt this page shows names the retained sealed decision log but gives no deletion date, and the explainer calls the retained assessment shell 'no personal data', so the candidate is told less, and something less accurate, than the standard requires about what survived.

techniques.evidence: app/data/[token]/DataClient.tsx:158 The held-data list renders only what the server projects from the actual entry (heldDataCategories in the route). A missing field renders nothing instead of the full template, and 'keptUntil' (line 245) is shown only when there is a parseable expiry.
messages/en.json:2081 The receipt names the retained type and its ground but no end date. The technique requires each retained record type to be named with its ground and the date it will be deleted.

messages/en.json:2075 It says 'de-identified', but then claims the retained shell holds 'no personal data'. The standard says pseudonymised data stays personal data for the organisation that holds it. This is 'anonymisation by adjective' on the candidate-facing surface.

app/data/[token]/DataClient.tsx:134 The page shows 'erased' only after a successful POST or after re-reading the real state (a 404 or anonymized=true). It never reports success optimistically, and it gives an in-place retry when the entry really is still there.
